summary: Binomial expansion modulo ℓ of p-th powers, then lifting the exponent from k to N.

steps.claim: For every a: ℓ divides (1 + x)^{ℓ^a} − 1 − x^{ℓ^a}, by the expansion of a sum to a prime power (add_pow_prime_pow_eq').
steps.lean: have H a := congr((ℓ : O) ∣ $(add_pow_prime_pow_eq' p.out 1 a k) - 1)

steps.claim: Rearranged: ℓ ∣ (1 + x)^{ℓ^a} − 1 iff ℓ ∣ x^{ℓ^a}.
The second claim follows from the first: if ℓ ∣ (1 + t(u − 1))^{ℓ^k} − 1, then ℓ^{N−k} divides its ℓ^{N−k}-th power minus 1 (dvd_sub_pow_of_dvd_sub), and M ≤ N − k.
steps.lean:
refine ⟨?t, by simpa [← pow_mul, ← pow_add, a.trans'] using
    (pow_dvd_pow _ (by lia)).trans (dvd_sub_pow_of_dvd_sub ((H _).2 ?t) (N - k))⟩

steps.claim: First claim: (t(u − 1))^{ℓ^k} = t^{ℓ^k}(u − 1)^{ℓ^k}, and ℓ divides (u − 1)^{ℓ^k} since (u − 1)^{ℓ^k} ≡ u^{ℓ^k} − 1 = 0 modulo ℓ (steps 1–2 with x = u − 1).
